A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 14-page versions of the same DCM-Agent paper. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and runtime experiments across seven optimization benchmarks, plus memory-transfer analyses, ablations, parameter sensitivity tests, and a case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4, Tables 2–6, and Figures 4–6.

M1.justification: The dual-cluster memory construction and memory-augmented generation, verification, repair, and backtracking procedures are unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2 in Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions report the same seven evaluation benchmarks and 500 memory-construction problems. v2 identifies the memory data's OptiVerse source and domains, without reporting replacement or expansion of the data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same standalone-model baseline, OptiMUS, AF-MCTS, and OptiTree comparisons. The new OptiVerse citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Benchmark sizes, backbone models, solving-accuracy criteria, allowed solver libraries, and parameter settings match. The new statement that memory problems were randomly sampled supplies a previously undisclosed selection detail; it does not establish a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.6 retain the same memory-budget and cross-model transfer analyses, cluster ablations, K/N/M sensitivity tests, and integrality case study. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting without evaluation confidence intervals or significance tests. No repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and findings in Tables 2–6 and Figures 4–6 match. For example, Table 2 retains the 71.28% reported average for DCM-Agent with Qwen3-235B; runtime, transfer, ablation, and sensitivity results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(9), including the graph, retrieval, and knowledge-update formulations. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free dual-cluster contribution, claimed 11%–21% average improvement, and cross-model knowledge-inheritance claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of memory transfer, cluster contributions, efficiency, and parameter sensitivity are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same memory-initialization cost limitation and proposed future online evolution.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 now specifies that the 500 memory problems were randomly sampled from OptiVerse's mathematical programming and combinatorial optimization domains. v1 left their source unspecified there. The count, disjointness statement, and appendix solver and annotation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhang et al. (2026), the OptiVerse benchmark paper, as a citation and bibliography entry supporting memory-data provenance. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The memory-data sentence in Section 4.1 is expanded, and the version/date stamp is updated. Section order and nearly all prose, including the appendices, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All six figures and six tables are retained. Added prose and the reference cause minor column/page reflow, including Appendix B continuing onto page 14 and the Appendix D heading shifting to the right column.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces the unspecified memory-data source in Section 4.1 with a cited source, named domains, and a sampling description. This modestly improves traceability of an important experimental input. The algorithms, empirical evidence, and substantive conclusions remain unchanged.
